clue.text: Sound of laughter from warmonger, cut short repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the shortened word is given twice in a row
cut short says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a hawk is a politician who favours war

explanation.surface: A sneering laugh comes from a belligerent politician, interrupted again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud guffaw, especially an affected or mocking one, is written as this reduplicated interjection.

clue.text: Cuts lines on graph

definitions.meaning: hatchets and choppers, the tools that cut wood
the x and y reference lines of a chart

explanation.definitionFit: The plural of axe (a chopping tool) and of axis (a chart's reference line) are spelt the same.

clue.text: Greeting Rosalind, then mother, in Asian city

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting
Ros is a short form of the name Rosalind
then implies the same greeting again, this time to mother: hi, plus ma for mother

explanation.surface: Saying hello to a friend and her mother in some city in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The greeting is used twice: HI ROS, then HI MA, part of the puzzle's doubles theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese port destroyed by the first atomic bomb in 1945 is a city in Asia.

clue.text: Did some work on plot in short act, half-heartedly

parts.note: wee means small or short

indicators.note: half-heartedly says one of the two middle letters goes

parts.note: a deed is an act

explanation.surface: A writer reworked the story within a brief scene without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a story; it is a garden plot. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearing unwanted plants out of a garden bed is gardening work on a plot of land.

clue.text: Drive off from established place for driving practice

parts.note: EST is the standard abbreviation for established, as on shop signs
a driving range is where golfers practise their long shots

explanation.surface: Someone is turned away from a golf practice ground that has long been in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like golf throughout, but in the definition it means to push someone away emotionally.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to drive them off, making them unfriendly or distant.

clue.text: OK with risky venture — in return, earn pile, possibly, after its end

indicators.note: after says the scrambled letters come after that end letter

parts.note: its refers to pile, whose last letter is E

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of return and earn pile may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A businessman happy to gamble hopes to get his money back and earn a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; RETURN and EARNPILE are anagrammed behind pile's final E.
explanation.definitionFit: A business founder is someone who takes on financial risk, so the adjective describes comfort with a gamble.

clue.text: Tool wasn't holding one up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the whole is read from bottom to top
holding says the contraction contains the number

parts.note: the contraction is spelt without its apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: An implement failed to support someone.
explanation.walkthrough: WASNT holding ONE gives WASNONET, which read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fine-toothed saw with a stiffened back is used by carpenters to cut joints.

clue.text: Attack incomplete, much seen in score

indicators.note: incomplete says the last letter is lost

parts.note: to assail is to attack

explanation.surface: An unfinished assault is clearly visible in the tally of points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like a match result; it is a piece of written music.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian word for very appears in tempo markings such as allegro assai, so it is seen in printed music.

clue.text: Eg concert I botched in relation to omission from The Planets

definitions.text: in relation to omission from The Planets

indicators.note: botched says the letters are messed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A performance of Holst's suite was spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: Holst's suite The Planets has no movement for Earth, the omission the definition points to.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to or centred on Earth, the world left out of the orchestral suite.

clue.text: Attention I needed in trial, being most distressed

indicators.note: needed in says the attention and the I are placed inside the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
to give someone your ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone under examination needs to be listened to while terribly upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word. This answer and 24 across are anagrams of each other, in matching grid places, part of the doubles theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of tearful-looking: the person crying most readily is the most upset.

clue.text: Wise counsellor somehow errs on no test, ignoring duplicates

indicators.note: somehow says the six surviving letters are rearranged
every letter of the phrase appears exactly twice, so ignoring duplicates keeps one copy of each

explanation.surface: A sage adviser somehow makes mistakes when there is no examination.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder ERRSONNOTEST has two each of E, R, S, O, N and T; one of each, ERSONT, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, the aged king of Pylos gives the Greek leaders advice, so his name means any wise old adviser.

clue.text: Seeing double, mistakenly means to invest

indicators.note: mistakenly says the doubled letters are put in the wrong order
double says the word is taken twice over

explanation.surface: Someone with double vision gets it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' here is the old military sense, to lay siege to a town, not to put money in.
explanation.definitionFit: Catapults and battering rams were the equipment used to besiege a fortified place.

clue.text: Heavenly body mostly struck that woman as alluring

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a comet is a heavenly body
struck means hit
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A shooting star mostly hit her and she found it attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A beckoning look or manner is inviting and seductive.

clue.text: Things like doughnuts, consumed more than once by motorist, originally

indicators.note: the four letters sit inside the two words twice: once across the middle of the first word and again running from its end into the next

explanation.surface: Doughnuts are eaten repeatedly by a driver at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The run appears in moTORIst and again in moTORIst ORIginally, overlapping, fitting the doubles theme.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a ring-shaped solid like a doughnut is a torus, and these are the plural.

clue.text: Over extended time, splits substances in chemical analysis

indicators.note: over says the splits are spread across, covering the extended time

parts.note: rents are tears or splits
an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Splits that last a long time are behind some lab work.
explanation.walkthrough: This answer and 5 across are anagrams of each other in matching grid places.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemists add a reactive compound to a sample to detect or measure another substance.

clue.text: By the way, stupidly pen stupid article on time

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the article above the time
stupidly says the letters of pen are put in a foolish order

parts.note: an ass is a fool
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A clumsy writer stupidly writes a silly item about time.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in passing, an aside or incidental remark.

clue.text: Covering wood with fine spray, was careless with hands

indicators.note: covering says the spray goes round the wood

parts.note: mist is a fine spray of droplets
deal is pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A worker spraying varnish on timber was sloppy with their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hands' are hands of cards, not fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer who gives out cards wrongly in a card game has made an error with the hands.

clue.text: Narrator's ultimate joy is storytelling

indicators.note: the narrator's ultimate is the final letter of that word

parts.note: elation is great joy

explanation.surface: The happy ending is what makes a storyteller's tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word. This answer and 25 across are anagrams of each other in matching grid places.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is an account or narration, as when one relates a story.

clue.text: This couple twice said to trim fruit tree

indicators.note: twice said to says the clue gives two words which each sound like the answer

parts.note: to pare is to trim, as with a knife

explanation.surface: Someone is told to prune a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit tree, a pear, sounds the same too, so the answer is heard twice, fitting the doubles theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is two of a kind, a twosome.

clue.text: Legal right in court for individual using lawyer?

indicators.note: in says the right goes inside the court

parts.note: a lien is a right to keep property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal right is upheld in court for someone who hires counsel.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who engages a solicitor's services is that solicitor's customer.

clue.text: Use bold arrangement that gender-balanced quartet plays

indicators.note: arrangement says the two words are a jumble, so they are to be read as a mixed-up version of a word

parts.note: the letters of use bold are the clue's other word scrambled, so they are that word in mixed form

explanation.surface: A designer is advised to set type in heavy face.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: the second word jumbled ('mixed') gives USE BOLD, the clue's opening.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis or badminton, a game with a man and a woman on each side is played by four people, two of each sex.

clue.text: Person who presents medal, as spelt out

indicators.note: as spelt out says the abbreviation is written as its letters are pronounced

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British gallantry medal

explanation.surface: Someone hands out an award, as was announced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Military Cross (MC) is a British army bravery award.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies introduces acts on a show, a host or compère.

clue.text: Before university, old boys getting information on courses

indicators.note: before says the men come ahead of the university

parts.note: men are males, here the old boys of a school

explanation.surface: Former pupils learn about degree courses before going to university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is a link word. 'courses' suggests study; it means the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare lists the dishes, starter, main and dessert, served in sequence.

clue.text: Dance music or rap endlessly reprised

indicators.note: reprised says the shortened word is given a second time
endlessly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to rap is to chat, talk informally

explanation.surface: A dance tune or a rap song keeps being repeated without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin American ballroom dance and the music written for it share this name.

clue.text: Repeats excerpt from writer, a testimony

indicators.note: excerpt from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone quotes back a passage from an author's sworn statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To say something again and again is to restate it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Zero cost for tenants, including one from distant region

parts.note: zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: including says the rental goes round the one

parts.note: rental is what tenants pay
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: No rent is charged to occupants, among them one who came from far away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orient is the Far East, so the adjective means coming from that faraway part of the world.

clue.text: Disapproval old king briefly echoed

indicators.note: echoed says the short name is heard twice
briefly says only the short form of the name is used

parts.note: the Egyptian pharaoh Tutankhamun is often called King Tut

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch, in short form, repeated his displeasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Clicking the tongue twice is the conventional sound of mild reproach or scolding.
